title: Politics, Markets & Power Plays - Systematic Investor 338

meta.source: Macro Transcripts/Politics, Markets & Power Plays - Systematic Investor 338.docx

speakers: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
summary: Top Traders Unplugged Systematic Investor 338: Jim gives a discretionary-macro/political-economy view with Niels hosting. Thesis: US administration is deliberately cutting demand to force the 10-year down and a Fed QE response, with a Nixon-1970s analogy; expects a 30-40% equity decline within 12-18 months, dollar pressure, debt monetisation, plus views on Europe rearmament, Taiwan risk, Turkey and long oil / gold calls.

coverage.note: Intro; American exceptionalism cracking, mean reversion, China free-trade stance
Crypto reserve, Bridgewater All Weather ETF, transactional world / populism
Trend-following performance update and index levels; Europe defence debt and bond yields; US stagflationary setup, refinancing wall
Administration strategy: cut demand to control 10-year, supply-side economics, budget cuts vs corporate tax cuts
Different timelines of demand cut vs supply side; GDP expectations; planned QE; liquidity and refinancing overhang
Dollar contradiction (strong dollar vs QE/austerity), markets bigger than policy, Nixon analogy
Nixon outcome, demographics and populism, two short-term paths for yields and markets
QE plus recession bad for markets, warning shot before bigger decline, Mar-a-Lago accord speculation
Debt jubilee / monetisation, Japan role, external debt share
Gold revaluation, Europe rearming and complacency
Europe wake-up call and crisis as catalyst
Taiwan/TSMC, China timing, Chinese equities call
What investors do with Taiwan risk; Nvidia liquidity and tail risk
Turkey: Russian support, rates, swing-player power loss, India
Syria theory, Turkish currency crisis view, Turkey importance to NATO
Oil and gold: long gold calls / short oil puts, oil bullish case
Oil in a market decline; market drop forces policy response; markets as fifth state
nothing actionable: outro and sponsor/rating plea

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: the crack in the armor of of kind of that American exceptionalism uh I think starting to see some other markets perform better
claims.claim: Non-US markets have started to outperform as the US-exceptionalism premium cracks.
claims.indicator: relative performance of non-US vs US equity markets
claims.direction: long non-US equities relative to US
claims.testable: partly: relative return series are testable, the regime call is discretionary

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: mean revert uh from some of these records uh in the years to come
claims.claim: US equity records are expected to mean revert over the coming years.
claims.testable: partly: mean-reversion from extremes is testable, timing is vague

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: President XI is kind of becoming a little bit of the anti-trump he's kind of really trying to fight for free trade
claims.claim: China is positioning as the free-trade advocate and pushing lower tariffs on trade partners while the US raises tariffs.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: we're moving to a world that is transactional that's essentially what what you said
claims.claim: The world is shifting from cooperative give-now-for-later-gain relations to transactional bargaining, driven by a transactional US leader.
claims.testable: no: regime description with no measurable signal

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: we are now seeing people just do things because they can not because it's the right thing to do
claims.claim: Power is being used simply because it can be, a broader populism-driven loss of norms with wide consequences.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: Bridgewater um I think has been working on coming out with their all- weather product uh in an ETF form uh with State Street
claims.claim: Bridgewater is bringing its All Weather risk-parity product to an ETF with State Street.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: it has been a a difficult few weeks uh in Trend following land mainly currencies us fixed income and US equities in particular has been kind of where the challenges uh have been
claims.claim: Trend followers had a difficult stretch in early 2025 with losses concentrated in currencies, US fixed income and US equities after reversals.
claims.conditions: after sharp reversals in currencies, bonds and equities
claims.testable: yes: trend index returns are public

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: Trend index is up 16 basis points but down almost 3% for the year
claims.claim: Trend index was about -3% YTD in mid-March 2025 while the equity index was -2.2% and the 20-year bond index was +4%, data points of a month when trend following lagged.
claims.indicator: SG Trend index, BTOP50, S&P 500 TR, MSCI World

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: my own Trend barometer finished at 50 that's kind of an improving uh level in the last few days
claims.claim: A proprietary trend barometer reading of 50 signals an improving trend environment after the drawdown.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: the wave of debt that's probably going to be um offered to pay for the uh expansion of there defense uh over here um is certainly having an impact on um long-term bond yields in Europe
claims.claim: Expected European defence-funding debt issuance pushes up long-term European bond yields, creating new trends.
claims.testable: yes: yield changes around fiscal announcements are measurable

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: there is a stagflationary setup right there's uh inflation was starting to break out as they come came in uh uh again the 10 year was breaking higher
claims.claim: Early 2025 had a stagflationary setup with inflation re-accelerating and the 10-year yield breaking higher, forcing monetary policy to consider going the other way than easing.
claims.testable: partly: yield and inflation series are testable, interpretation is narrative

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: the five-year anniversary of the low in interest rates and a massive bubble of refinancing
claims.claim: A refinancing wall arrives about five years after the 2020 rate lows (venture, private equity, commercial real estate) with bankruptcies ticking up, a liquidity drain.
claims.conditions: 3 to 6 months out from the talk
claims.testable: yes: maturity walls and default data are public

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: we need to get demand down we need to get the 10year under control first priority only priority for them right now
claims.claim: The administration's stated top priority is lowering the 10-year yield, which it pursues by removing demand.
claims.testable: partly: policy intent is inferred from statements

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: if you send money to the top it's not inflationary those people don't spend it asset inflationary and asset inflation actually reflexively pushes uh kind of demand in the whole system
claims.claim: Supply-side policy that sends money to the top is not consumer-inflationary but inflates assets, which reflexively lifts demand and capital at the top.
claims.testable: partly: wealth-effect and marginal-propensity-to-consume claims are testable

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: those are all taking directly away from demand
claims.claim: Cuts to food aid, housing support, school lunches, Medicaid, federal jobs and Ukraine payments directly remove demand from lower and middle income cohorts.
claims.testable: partly: fiscal impulse is measurable, the intent is inferred

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: they're continuing the massive cut tax cut for corporations um 90% of those tax cuts go to corporations
claims.claim: Corporate tax cuts and deregulation are the offsetting supply-side stimulus, which acts slowly.
claims.testable: partly: lag from tax cuts to growth is testable

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: those two things don't work on the same timeline um the the demand removal you take checks that people were getting away next month that money just isn't there and it cuts demand dramatically
claims.claim: Demand removal acts within a month while supply-side stimulus takes years, so a short-term growth air pocket results.
claims.direction: US growth down first, supply response later
claims.testable: partly: lags of fiscal cuts vs tax cuts are testable

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: we've seen GDP expectations for the first quarter in the US go from around three and a half% positive to almost 3% negative in like two months
claims.claim: Q1 2025 US GDP nowcasts fell from about +3.5% to about -3% in two months, evidence of rapid demand loss.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: they really are looking to manufacture a decline in markets and the economy uh to get to force the fat on board
claims.claim: The administration wants markets and the economy to fall so the Fed is forced to stop QT and ease.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: perent has been quoted maybe 20 times at this point saying six to 12 months
claims.claim: Treasury Secretary Bessent repeatedly cites a six to 12 month timeline, which Jim reads as the time to a QE-type response.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: markets themselves reflexively take out liquidity from the system and uh you have to respond with a lot of QE to to move things
claims.claim: Falling markets drain liquidity reflexively, so a large QE response is needed to offset them, and the Fed may not be willing or quick enough.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: a massive refinancing uh reinvestment cycle where liquidity is kind of coming off the table
claims.claim: Simultaneous IPO, VC, private-equity and commercial real estate refinancing needs absorb liquidity and can overwhelm Fed counteraction.
claims.conditions: starting 3 to 6 months out

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: they want a strong dollar all of a sudden right they're being very vocal about that
claims.claim: US officials want a strong dollar, yet austerity combined with QE and lower rates usually weakens a currency; the contradiction is the strategy's weak point.
claims.conditions: if US growth falls while the rest of the world holds up and QE plus lower rates arrive
claims.testable: partly: dollar response to QE/rate cuts is testable

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: sometimes the markets are bigger than than you can manage
claims.claim: Markets can overwhelm official attempts to manage yields, the dollar and volatility.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: markets are relatively efficient and you can try and manipulate and and try and do X Y and Z but Market adjustments on the other side
claims.claim: Manipulating one price (yields) gets offset by market adjustment elsewhere (the dollar) unless the economy is a closed system like China.
claims.conditions: only a closed capital system can control rebalancing

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: Nixon came in as a republican he said look this inflation's a problem I need to do supply side economics what he do he opened up China he took us off he did Breton Woods
claims.claim: Nixon-era analogy: supply-side policy plus ending Bretton Woods and loosening monetary policy under Arthur Burns preceded the 1970s inflation, and the current administration is seen as repeating it.
claims.testable: partly: historical analogy of one episode

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: the real push to inflation started during Nixon
claims.claim: Inflation took off under Nixon after earlier easing, linking policy mix to the inflation regime.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: we had a recession in 6970 um so you know we saw this and and how did it work out well ended in price control
claims.claim: In the Nixon analogy, a 1969-70 recession and aggressive monetary support ended in price controls and political anger; populist response followed.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: baby boomers die and millennials increasingly becoming the dominant political force
claims.claim: Demographic turnover from boomers to millennials makes populism a 10 to 15 year theme that policies cannot easily reverse.
claims.conditions: populist wave plays out over 10 to 15 years

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: the 10year then goes back above five relatively quickly and I think that's the one thing nobody thinks is possible right now
claims.claim: Path two: after QE during a recession, the 10-year yield could return above 5% as a heavy refinancing demand for debt coincides; Jim rates this higher probability than expected.
claims.conditions: after aggressive QE coincides with refinancing demand
claims.testable: partly: price level testable but a one-off forecast

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: the 10-year continues to come down as GDP responds even worse than expected
claims.claim: Path one: the 10-year keeps falling as growth disappoints and QE is too small, so markets fade in a deeper recession than expected.
claims.conditions: if QE response is too small

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: the QE response I mean that's really bad that's even worse for markets
claims.claim: A recession followed by QE and a rising 10-year is even worse for markets, giving a knee-jerk rally that then fails.
claims.conditions: when QE coincides with rising long yields
claims.testable: partly: event-study of QE in recessions

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: a warning shot which we often see before a bigger move months before a bigger move
claims.claim: A February-March pullback is a warning shot that often precedes a much bigger decline by months, as seen in 1999 and 2007.
claims.conditions: preceding bigger declines
claims.testable: partly: precursor drawdown pattern is testable

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: I do think a bigger one is coming and I think it's coming in this year um or sometime in the next call it 12 to 18 months
claims.claim: A larger-than-10-20% equity decline is expected within the next 12 to 18 months.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: the US can't do it fully alone as much as it likes to think it can at some point the rest of the world combined is bigger than the US
claims.claim: A Mar-a-Lago-style accord forcing allies to buy 100-year zero-coupon US bonds is speculative; the US cannot bully the world indefinitely.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: we're going to monetize our debt in in some form or another there's only there's only one way out
claims.claim: The US will eventually monetize its debt in some form (a slow-rolling debt jubilee), protected by the dollar's reserve privilege, as Japan did.
claims.indicator: central bank holdings of government debt
claims.testable: partly: debt monetisation and inflation are testable, the call is long dated

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: there's going to be some cancellation of external debt from Japan you can bet bet your life on that
claims.claim: Jim expects Japan and its central bank to play a major role in cancelling or restructuring part of the US external debt.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: it's 27% of of US debt is external
claims.claim: Only about 27% of US debt is held externally, so most restructuring would have to be internal.
claims.indicator: share of US debt held by foreigners

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: I think it's a slow rolling train wreck
claims.claim: Debt resolution would be a slow process rather than a one-off event.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: revalue the price of gold in all your the the book value of your gold
claims.claim: Revaluing the book value of central-bank gold is floated as a way to ease the debt position.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: Gold's not as relevant as it used to be
claims.claim: Gold's relevance for solving US debt is limited today.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: this is for Germany alone it's a potential expansion of 10 to 20% of GDP
claims.claim: European rearmament could be a fiscal expansion of 10 to 20% of GDP for Germany alone.
claims.testable: partly: size of fiscal impulse is measurable

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: has depended on the US way too much all right um It's Made It complacent
claims.claim: Europe's reliance on the US made it complacent and unwilling to make hard decisions; the defence shock forces resilience.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: crisis brings people together we've talked about this again again like you kind of need crisis to to to get things moving in a good direction
claims.claim: Crisis is needed to catalyse reform in Europe, so the rearmament shock is painful short-term but good longer-term.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: Europe more likely out of the mud
claims.claim: Rearmament and harder decisions are expected to get Europe out of its stagnation.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: this will maybe also change uh the appetite from the us to come in and defend Taiwan
claims.claim: Large TSMC US investments may reduce the US appetite to defend Taiwan.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: that's part of why we kind of gave the big green light on Chinese equities
claims.claim: A softening of US-China rhetoric after the election was one reason Jim turned bullish on Chinese equities.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: I honestly think that could be this this Q4 of this year
claims.claim: China could move on Taiwan (embargo or pressure rather than military) around Q4 2025, once the Ukraine deal is done and the US is in recession.
claims.conditions: if the US is in recession and Ukraine settled

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: Taiwan if you if you want help from us you better pay for it
claims.claim: Trump's July 2024 'pay for protection' remarks on Taiwan started a volatility episode and the August dip.
claims.testable: partly: event study of the remark

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen (host; caption "Neil costr Larson")
claims.quote: even if you know what the event is it's sometimes very surprising in terms of what how the markets react
claims.claim: Even when the event is foreseen, market reaction can be counterintuitive (for example 10-year yields rose after the Fed cut).

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: if the market goes down that liquidity will be a problem to Nvidia the spend which has been dramatic there will come will get pulled back very quickly
claims.claim: Nvidia's growth depends on AI capex that would be pulled back quickly in a market decline, so its growth expectations could fall as fast as they rose.
claims.conditions: in a market decline

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: it seems like it's an obvious buy yet it keeps going down maybe you should be careful
claims.claim: When everyone is bullish and an obvious buy keeps falling, caution is warranted since there may be a risk not being considered (a Taiwan tail risk).
claims.conditions: when consensus is bullish and price keeps falling

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: imagine a scenario where you know Nvidia is swooning still it continues to Swoon as the market does
claims.claim: Forced liquidation of crowded leadership stocks while a Taiwan shock arrives would amplify downside; be mindful of tail risk in crowded longs.
claims.conditions: leadership stocks in forced selling

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: Russia was sending oil uh and and gas to Turkey for free basically
claims.claim: Russia has supplied Turkey energy on credit, building a debt Putin can call as leverage.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: all of a sudden who loses power in that situation it's the swing players
claims.claim: If Russia and the West reconcile, swing states like Turkey and India lose bargaining power and market support.
claims.conditions: a US-Russia thaw

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: the way he's built his economy is essentially running really loose monetary policy
claims.claim: Erdogan's preference for loose monetary policy conflicts with 40% rates, so keeping rates high as conditions worsen is doubtful.
claims.conditions: if political pressure overrides the central bank

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: it's not a surprise that Indian markets have not been doing well
claims.claim: Indian equities were hurt by prior excitement and loss of swing-state value; Turkey is worse as its economy is already weak.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: I think there's a decent chance of of a currency crisis in Turkey
claims.claim: A Turkish currency crisis is a decent chance given the weak economy, upcoming elections and Russia pressure.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: I have a theory that that the Biden Administration who essentially removed Military Support
claims.claim: Theory: the Biden administration let Turkish-backed forces take Damascus to give Turkey a counterweight to Russia in Syria.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: is to buy gold calls and sell oil puts and those are very different ways to be long of an asset right
claims.claim: A trade that worked for 3.5 years: buy gold calls and sell oil puts, because gold was under-priced in volatility and oil over-priced; both assets perform in a decade-long inflationary, deglobalising environment.
claims.direction: long gold calls, short oil puts
claims.conditions: when oil vol is high after a rally and gold vol is low

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: it's going to be the one that is much more volatile in the trade
claims.claim: Gold, not oil, is expected to be the more volatile of the two over the longer run.
claims.direction: long gold vol / short oil vol

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: I think oil has supply issues that will support it um it also has geopolitical you know uh you know deglobalization global conflict that help underpin it
claims.claim: Oil is bullish multi-year due to supply issues, geopolitics and deglobalisation, despite drill-baby-drill pressure.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: is in for potential for the first time in a while right uh in for some potential pain and if that's the case that's very supportive of oil
claims.claim: A weaker dollar and China demand recovery would be supportive of oil even in a US recession.
claims.conditions: dollar falls

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: you know gold is a is a currency uh you know gold is a is a is not a industrial commodity
claims.claim: Gold behaves as a currency rather than an industrial commodity and is unrelated to demand cycles, unlike oil.
claims.testable: partly: cyclical beta of gold is testable

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: markets come down in the next year and energy actually kind of hangs in
claims.claim: Energy holds up during the equity decline and then outperforms coming out of it.
claims.conditions: during an equity decline
claims.testable: partly: sector behaviour in drawdowns testable

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: if the market drops 40% which I think it
claims.claim: A 30-40% equity decline over the next year and a half is expected and would pressure policymakers to change course.

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: there's going to be a response by people are going to be a little bit less friendly to uh the administration
claims.claim: A large market fall leads to political backlash (job losses, wealthy donors) and policy reversal, as with Nixon's price controls.
claims.conditions: after a deep market decline
claims.testable: partly: market-to-policy feedback is testable via event study

claims.speaker: Jim (guest, systematic macro investor; caption "Jim kasang")
claims.quote: I do think markets will become a check on Donald Trump in this Administration
claims.claim: Markets are a 'fifth state' that check government policy; a market lead on political outcomes.
claims.testable: partly: policy changes after drawdowns testable
